blockers: switching costs and meal continuity risk
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A remediation plan may coexist temporarily with rebid preparation, so short-run corrective steps do not negate this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: The district initiates a formal rebid or equivalent competitive replacement process that results in the incumbent losing control of the meal contract.
endpoint_ledger.label: formal_rebid_and_vendor_replacement

meta.important_question: Does the district ultimately keep the incumbent vendor under the challenged contract, replace it through rebid, or terminate it through emergency action?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Rebid is a terminal option if evidence strengthens and process constraints can be managed.
realization_criteria: district publicly or formally issues rebid/solicitation or equivalent competitive replacement action
incumbent is not retained as the continuing primary meal vendor after award decision
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly names rebid as a possible branch, but no formal procurement action is yet described at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If remediation is purely rhetorical and quickly collapses into cancellation or rebid, this endpoint is not realized.
endpoint_ledger.description: The district keeps the incumbent vendor in place under an explicit corrective action framework with measurable oversight.
endpoint_ledger.label: incumbent_retained_under_monitored_remediation

meta.important_question: Is the district response publicly visible and formalized, or mostly handled through low-visibility administrative process?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The district has incentives to preserve continuity while buying time under procurement constraints.
realization_criteria: district and vendor adopt documented corrective benchmarks or oversight milestones
incumbent continues service beyond the immediate dispute period without formal replacement or emergency termination
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Vendor defense and continuity pressures make remediation the most immediate nonterminal mechanism available at T0.

blockers: administrative reluctance to risk service disruption
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Escalated rhetoric alone does not realize this endpoint without formal action and operational substitution.
endpoint_ledger.description: The district invokes emergency or expedited authority to end or suspend the incumbent arrangement before a standard renewal or rebid conclusion.
endpoint_ledger.label: emergency_cancellation_or_suspension

meta.important_question: If remediation is chosen, does it become a real monitored corrective regime or a symbolic delay mechanism before renewal or replacement?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint becomes more likely if quality concerns are reframed as urgent safety or repeated operational breakdown.
realization_criteria: district formally cancels, suspends, or materially halts incumbent contract under emergency or exception authority
interim meal sourcing is shifted away from incumbent through emergency measures
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario names emergency cancellation as a possible path, but T0 evidence does not yet establish extreme threshold conditions.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A temporary remediation announcement may still culminate in quiet renewal if monitoring fades and no terminal switch occurs.
endpoint_ledger.description: The incumbent relationship is quietly renewed or extended with limited public confrontation and weak visible change.
endpoint_ledger.label: low_visibility_renewal_or_extension

meta.important_question: Do parents, students, and union-linked staff sustain a pressure coalition long enough to influence the terminal contract outcome?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Administrative inertia and market dependence can favor continuation if public salience drops.
realization_criteria: district approves or executes renewal/extension of incumbent arrangement
no substantial public-facing accountability process or competitive replacement interrupts the continuation
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly includes quiet renewal as a branch; continuity incentives and attention decay make it plausible though contested.

Final authority between board, district administration, and procurement office is inferred but not explicitly specified in the corpus.
Alternative vendor availability is central to endpoint probabilities but not evidenced directly.
Nutritionist memo and union note could sharply shift public legitimacy if disclosed across channels.
Public pressure may underestimate meal service switching costs, creating divergence between preferred and feasible endpoints.

internal staff capacity limits vs outsourcing dependence
simulation_brief.summary: A fictional school meal vendor contract faces challenge after allegations of poor food quality and late deliveries. Initial evidence sources include parent emails, vendor defense statements, a nutritionist memo, student posts, a union kitchen staff note, and procurement rules. Terminal pressure centers on whether the district pursues rebid, remediation, emergency cancellation, or quiet renewal.
simulation_brief.title: fictional_school_meal_vendor_contract_dispute
uncertainty_notes: Full source corpus is summarized rather than fully reproduced.
Specific district size, contract value, and documented violation counts are not provided.
Some actors and counts are inferred at a realistic fictional district scale to support T0 simulation.
